items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I heard you talking to Andre Previn. And the two of you were discussing Art Tatum,

ctx.x: Well speaking of the word “inspiration,” I think I’m a good example of it, because I was removed from the roots of it. I came from Montreal as you know, and although it was a jazz center in Canada, it was well removed from New York, Kansas City or St. Louis or Chicago. And I had to get my background in jazz intravenously so to speak, through the radio and recordings. That was the only way I could, you know, I could ingest what was going on, was to listen to the radio at night.

I did as well, you know. I heard you talking to Andre Previn. And the two of you were discussing Art Tatum, and you were telling a story I thought was marvelous, about the first time you heard him. Your father brought home recordings?

Yeah. I was studying classical piano, and I was doing pretty good at it. And I was also into the jazz scene a little bit, and I was getting pretty cocky, you know, because at that time I could outplay most of my fellow students in the jazz scene. And my father sensed this, and he had a, he knew a tenor saxophone player by the name of George Sealy who had a record collection. And he showed up this day, he brought George Sealy home with him, and he said, “hey I’ve got something for you to hear.” I said, “yeah? What…
